assessment.rationale: Nothing records human brain activity non-invasively at cell resolution, so the Main KPI of one non-invasive cell-level recorder is unmet and the project is open work. A targeted review search found no method that does it: the cellular-resolution claims belong to intraoperative optical imaging in glioblastoma surgery, to retinal imaging where a non-invasive label-free cellular-resolution clinical system resolves neurovascular coupling in the living human retina (Sci Adv 2025), or to optogenetics, which needs gene delivery and is not a recording method (https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/search?query=%22cellular%20resolution%22%20AND%20noninvasive%20AND%20%22human%20brain%22%20AND%20review&format=json&pageSize=5&resultType=core). Broader queries return 349 and 60 records whose relevant content is adjacent rather than on target: quantum sensing for epilepsy diagnostics, transcranial focused ultrasound modulating primate thalamic spiking, zebrafish functional networks, and a 2019 brain-cloud-interface speculation. The nearest open-source work is functional ultrasound in animals, four repositories led by whole-brain fUS in awake head-fixed mice with 23 stars (https://api.github.com/search/repositories?q=functional+ultrasound+imaging+brain&per_page=10&sort=stars). Honest limits: functional ultrasound, optically pumped magnetometer MEG and diffuse optics are published and partly open, so a task that only re-runs one of them is a known answer; and no source found here quantifies the physical ceiling set by skull scattering, depth and the haemodynamic rather than spiking nature of the signal, which a task should establish before promising cell resolution.

additionalSearches.query: non-invasive cellular-resolution human brain recording reviews
additionalSearches.finding: No record establishes non-invasive single-cell recording in the human brain. Cellular-resolution claims are for intraoperative optical imaging in glioblastoma (probe delivery across the blood-brain barrier cited as a limit) and for the living human retina (Sci Adv 2025); optogenetics is an intervention requiring gene delivery. None states the physical limits for the brain.

additionalSearches.query: non-invasive single-neuron whole-brain human recording literature
additionalSearches.finding: 349 hits whose returned sample contains no non-invasive single-neuron human method: shallow recurrent decoders, quantum sensing for epilepsy diagnostics, transcranial focused ultrasound modulating primate thalamic spiking and LFP, neuroprosthesis reviews. The gap is not filled by anything indexed.

additionalSearches.query: functional ultrasound and MEG cellular resolution claims
additionalSearches.finding: 60 hits; the only cellular-resolution items are animal (zebrafish functional networks) or speculative (Human Brain/Cloud Interface, Front Neurosci 2019), with the rest intraoperative or optogenetic. No human non-invasive cellular recording is reported.

Four repositories, all animal: whole-brain functional ultrasound in awake head-fixed mice (23 stars), a processing toolkit for developing mouse and non-human-primate brains, emotion correlates in mice, and a drug-response analysis. No open system records human neurons non-invasively.
